answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because prism only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, juniper is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any cedar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
